messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: sudden increase in NVIDIA Xid48 and Xid79 errors across us-east1-rack-7 and eu-west1-rack-2. 40 events in last 12m. Affected nodes: rdw-e07-*-gpu. Severity: P3.
jordan: pinging eng-sre, this looks like a mixed Xid signature. any immediate mitigation?
maya: seeing correlation with small-batch embedder workloads (embedder-light). they spike token-by-token and keep GPUs hot. nvlog attached to alert shows repeated NVLINK peer resets + ECC corrections.
siva: can you paste the snippet?
maya: ```
[ 12:02:41 ] Xid 79: GPU HANG, engine timeout
[ 12:02:42 ] NVLINK: peer reset on link 1
[ 12:02:42 ] ECC: single-bit corrected error on GPU 1
[ 12:03:05 ] Xid 48: GPU reset during kernel execution
```
liam: interesting — NVLINK resets + ECC single-bit corrective pattern often indicates thermal cycling or a flaky GPU DIMM/vbios issue, not just driver.
karim: I also see periodic fan PWM oscillation on rdw-e07-12 (temp swings 70C -> 60C -> 72C in <60s). could be a control loop bug causing sudden throttles -> NVLINK resyncs.
jordan: OK immediate plan: 1) drain the two most noisy hosts (rdw-e07-12, rdw-e07-15) from serving, 2) move embedder-light traffic to dedicated pool in us-west, 3) collect full dmesg + nvidia-smi dmon, 4) schedule remote power cycle + run nv-hostengine diag and ECC stress. agree? @oncall
oncall: acknowledged, starting drain now. will redirect embeddings to fallback pool (dedicated-embedder-temp) with gradual shift 20% -> 100% to avoid cold start spike. :thumbsup:
siva: I'll attach the quick query used to map Xid events to tenants: ```sql
select tenant, count(*) from gpu_xid_events where xid in (48,79) and ts > now() - interval '1 hour' group by tenant order by 2 desc;
```
maya: result shows 65% of events tied to tenant-id T-438 (heavy small-batch embed) and 20% to internal eval harness. others are spread.
liam: long-term: consider dedicated capacity for T-438. They push many small concurrent sessions which increases thermal churn and kernel preemption. Dedicated pool would reduce cross-tenant noisy neighbour issues and give us control over batch sizes. cost tradeoffs to ops and account team.
karim: hardware suspects: two cards show persistent corrected ECC counts incrementing beyond baseline and nv-hostengine reports "persistently high correctable ECC" on one GPU. recommend RMA for those two cards after power cycle confirms.
jordan: agreed. action items assigned: 
- @oncall: complete drain + redirect (in progress)
- @maya: collect and upload dmesg, nvidia-smi logs to /internal/triage/1718204321/ (include nv-hostengine output)
- @siva: run targeted stress (memtest + ECC repro) on drained cards and post results
- @liam: draft short note to account team for tenant T-438 recommending dedicated pool (include cost delta)
Estimated timeline: 3-6 hours for repro and decision.
maya: uploaded logs: https://internal.storage/redwood/triage/1718204321/logs.tar.gz. includes per-second dmon, temp traces, and nv-hostengine dump.
siva: did the stress run on rdw-e07-12 after soft power cycle: memtest produced 3 corrected ECC events within 30m and then one Xid48 during heavy kernel churn. copying log to upload. conclusion: likely flaky card, not just cooling.
liam: I'll queue RMA for rdw-e07-12 and rdw-e07-15 once oncall confirms post-power-cycle state. also keeping a temporary tag on those hosts to avoid scheduling critical jobs until replaced.
karim: quick note for ops: check motherboard BIOS for fan control firmware — PWM oscillation was weird. I recommend updating BMC firmware if RMA doesn't fix it.
jordan: good catch. any objections to switching the offending tenant to dedicated this afternoon?
oncall: no objections, doing gradual cutover now. will report back when traffic at 100% on dedicated pool. ETA ~45m.
maya: after initial drain we saw Xid events drop by ~80% on rack-7 within 10m. still seeing residual on rack-2 eu-west but fewer.
siva: I'll follow up with hardware vendor on the ECC signature and NVLINK resets, include dmesg excerpt and nv-hostengine dump.
jordan: thanks team. I'll update incident tracker with triage notes and link the logs. If RMA confirmed, schedule replacement during low-traffic window (00:00-04:00 UTC). Closing loop once cards replaced. :white_check_mark:
